headline: Retaining wall repair at 5 Sunrise Drive on Ramshorn Pond debated as emergency; work may wait until the 18th.
summary: The engineer said the wall by Ramshorn Pond is falling toward the lake, and repairs must happen while the water is low. The plan rebuilds the wall in the same spot and height, with stone on the existing foundation. Some members said the work did not qualify as an emergency. The applicant hopes to start while the weather holds, and the RDA is on the 18th agenda. The commission also issued a certificate of compliance for 345 Central Turnpike.
decisions: Approved a complete certificate of compliance for 345 Central Turnpike, DEP number 303-0962, 5-0.
discussion: 5 Sunrise Drive wall repair: The engineer said the poured concrete wall is falling toward the lake and would be rebuilt in the same spot and height. Some members said the work was not an emergency, while others said the good weather favored starting soon.
14 Davis Circle complaint follow-up: Members said aerial images since 1990 show the retaining wall and boat ramp area in the same location. No written complaint had been seen.

38 Southwick Road monitoring: The site review found well over 75% survival of native plants and no invasive species in the replication area. The reviewer recommended that the owner request a certificate of compliance.

320 Putnam Hill site work: The owners said trees were cleared and piled for chipping, and they asked whether to plant now or wait for spring. Members said the site looked stable and set a June 1 target to finish, with a letter confirming completion at the first June meeting.
45 Stoneschool Road plantings: The site visit found the 34 required plantings appear to be missing. The reviewer recommended continuing the item until the plantings are confirmed.
